storage.definition: S(r) = |r| bits. The memory required to store the representation.
storage.relation_to_C: S(r) ≥ K(f) ≤ C(f). Storage is bounded by K, not C.
storage.tag: [PROVEN] Storage advantage REQUIRES compression. K(f) is the bound.

time.definition: T(r) = number of sequential steps to execute r on one processor.
time.relation_to_K: K(f) bounds storage, NOT time. A short program can be slow (K small, T large).
time.relation_to_C: T(r) ≥ C(f)/p for p processors. Circuit complexity is the time bound.
time.counterexample_without_compression: Parallel decomposition: f = g ∘ h, T_par = max(T(g),T(h)) < T(g)+T(h) = T_seq. |g|+|h| = |f| (no compression). [PROVEN + MEASURED]
time.tag: [PROVEN] Time advantage does NOT require compression. Parallelism provides speedup without compression.

depth.definition: D(r) = longest path in the execution DAG (critical path length).
depth.relation_to_K: No direct relation to K(f). Depth is a structural property.
depth.relation_to_C: D(r) ≤ C(r). Depth ≤ circuit size. NC class: poly-size, polylog-depth.
depth.counterexample_without_compression: Balanced tree evaluation: D = O(log d) vs sequential D = O(d). Same function, same size, different depth. [PROVEN]
depth.tag: [PROVEN] Depth advantage does NOT require compression. Tree balancing reduces depth without changing size.

work.definition: W(r) = total number of primitive operations (gate count).
work.relation_to_K: W(r) ≥ K(f). Fewer ops requires a shorter program. [PROVEN]
work.tag: [PROVEN] Work advantage REQUIRES compression. W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f).

communication.definition: Comm(r) = bits transmitted between processors during distributed execution.
communication.relation_to_K: Communication can be reduced by locality (rearranging computation), not compression.
communication.relation_to_C: Comm depends on the partition, not the circuit size.
communication.counterexample_without_compression: Cache-oblivious algorithms: same computation, different memory layout → less communication. No compression. [PROVEN]
communication.tag: [PROVEN] Communication advantage does NOT require compression. Locality reduces communication without reducing description length.

verification_cost.definition: V_cost(r) = cost to verify that r computes f correctly.
verification_cost.relation_to_K: Verification cost is independent of K(f). A short program can be expensive to verify.
verification_cost.relation_to_C: V_cost can be less than C(f) via probabilistic checking (PCP theorem).
verification_cost.counterexample_without_compression: PCP theorem: verify with O(log n) queries instead of O(n). No compression of f — just more efficient verification. [PROVEN]
verification_cost.tag: [PROVEN] Verification advantage does NOT require compression. PCP theorem enables sublinear verification.

parallelism.definition: P(r) = number of processors that can be usefully employed.
parallelism.relation_to_K: Parallelism is structural (DAG width), not informational.
parallelism.counterexample_without_compression: Any parallel algorithm: same work, more processors, less time. No compression. [PROVEN]
parallelism.tag: [PROVEN] Parallelism advantage does NOT require compression.

locality.definition: L(r) = cache misses / memory transfers during execution.
locality.relation_to_K: Locality is a data layout property, not a description length property.
locality.relation_to_C: L depends on memory hierarchy, not circuit size.
locality.counterexample_without_compression: Matrix multiply: same computation, blocked layout → O(√n) cache misses vs O(n). No compression. [PROVEN]
locality.tag: [PROVEN] Locality advantage does NOT require compression.

synchronization.definition: Sync(r) = number of barrier synchronizations during parallel execution.
synchronization.relation_to_K: Synchronization is an algorithmic structure property.
synchronization.relation_to_C: Sync depends on the parallel schedule, not the circuit.
synchronization.counterexample_without_compression: Asynchronous algorithms: same computation, fewer barriers. No compression. [PROVEN]
synchronization.tag: [PROVEN] Synchronization advantage does NOT require compression.

amortization.definition: Amort(r, n) = total cost / n for n uses of r.
amortization.relation_to_K: Amortization requires |r| < |O| (A3). The law must be cheaper than repeated direct computation.
amortization.relation_to_C: Amort = (C_D + C_V + n·C_E) / n. Advantage requires C_E < C_direct.
amortization.tag: [PROVEN] Amortization advantage REQUIRES compression. Without |r| < |O|, amortization is never positive.

storage_advantage.definition: |r| < |O| — the representation is smaller than the raw data.
storage_advantage.sufficient_condition: K(f) < |O| AND D finds r with |r| ≈ K(f)

time_advantage.definition: T(r) < T(f_direct) — execution is faster than direct computation.
time_advantage.sufficient_condition: C(r) < C(f_direct) (smaller circuit implies faster sequential execution)
time_advantage.relation_to_K: Neither necessary nor sufficient. K small doesn't imply T small.
time_advantage.relation_to_parallel: T = W/P = C/P. Parallelism reduces T without reducing C. [PROVEN]
time_advantage.tag: [PROVEN] Time advantage does NOT require compression. Parallelism suffices.

work_advantage.sufficient_condition: C(r) < C(f_direct) AND r computes f correctly
work_advantage.relation_to_K: W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f). Work advantage IS compression advantage. [PROVEN]
work_advantage.relation_to_parallel: Work is invariant under parallelism (Brent: W = T×P).
work_advantage.tag: [PROVEN] Work advantage = compression advantage. W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f).

depth_advantage.sufficient_condition: Balanced decomposition with D = O(log W)
depth_advantage.tag: [PROVEN] Depth advantage does NOT require compression. Tree balancing suffices.

communication_advantage.relation_to_parallel: Communication is the bottleneck in distributed computing. [PROVEN]
communication_advantage.tag: [PROVEN] Communication advantage does NOT require compression. Locality suffices.

verification_advantage.sufficient_condition: PCP theorem: O(log n) queries suffice
verification_advantage.relation_to_C: V_cost can be << C(f) via PCP. [PROVEN]
verification_advantage.tag: [PROVEN] Verification advantage does NOT require compression. PCP suffices.

storage_theorem.statement:
Under A1, A2, A4, every STORAGE advantage requires compact representation + verification + execution.
S(r) ≥ K(f). Storage advantage requires S(r) < |O|, hence K(f) < |O|.
storage_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] This is the original closure theorem. It is CORRECT for storage.

work_theorem.statement:
Under A1, A2, A4, every WORK advantage requires compact representation + verification + execution.
W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f). Work advantage requires C(r) < C(f_direct), hence K(f) < C(f_direct).
work_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] Work advantage = storage advantage. Same bound K(f).

time_theorem.statement:
Under A1, A2, A4, every TIME advantage requires EITHER (a) compact representation (C(r) < C(f_direct)) OR (b) parallel decomposition (P > 1 with same C).
Compression is SUFFICIENT but NOT NECESSARY.
T(r) ≥ C(r)/P. Time advantage requires C(r)/P < C(f_direct).
time_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] Time advantage does NOT require compression. Parallelism (b) provides time advantage without compression.

depth_theorem.statement:
Under A1, A2, A4, every DEPTH advantage requires parallelizable structure (DAG width > 1). Compression is NOT necessary.
D(r) ≥ log₂(C(r)) for balanced circuits. Depth advantage requires D(r) < D(f_direct).
depth_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] Depth advantage does NOT require compression. Tree balancing reduces depth without changing size.

communication_theorem.statement:
Under A1, A2, A4, every COMMUNICATION advantage requires better data locality or partition. Compression is NOT necessary.
Comm(r) depends on the memory layout, not the description length.
communication_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] Communication advantage does NOT require compression. Locality (cache-oblivious algorithms) suffices.

verification_theorem.statement:
Under A1, A2, A4, every VERIFICATION COST advantage requires probabilistic checking or structure exploitation. Compression is NOT necessary.
V_cost(r) can be O(log n) via PCP theorem, independent of |r|.
verification_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] Verification cost advantage does NOT require compression. PCP theorem enables sublinear verification.

core_answer.question: When a system gains advantage by parallel decomposition, locality, or hardware structure, is that: A. computation reduction, B. execution optimization, C. different computational model, or D. resource-specific advantage?
core_answer.answer: D — resource-specific advantage that cannot be reduced to compression.
core_answer.proof:
Parallel decomposition of f = g ∘ h provides:
  - Same storage: |g| + |h| = |f| (no compression)
  - Same work: W(g) + W(h) = W(f) (no op reduction)
  - Less time: T_par = max(T(g), T(h)) < T(g) + T(h) = T_seq
  - Less depth: D_par = max(D(g), D(h)) < D(g) + D(h) = D_seq

This is NOT computation reduction (same work, same storage).
This is NOT merely an implementation detail (it changes the resource profile).
This is NOT a different computational model (same function, same circuit).
It IS a resource-specific advantage: the TIME resource is reduced by parallelism, without reducing the WORK or STORAGE resources.

The advantage is REAL (measured in wall-clock time) but it is ORTHOLOGONAL to compression. Compression reduces STORAGE and WORK. Parallelism reduces TIME and DEPTH. These are independent axes.

final_verdict.original_theorem: Under A1-A4, every computational advantage requires compact representation + verification + execution.
final_verdict.verdict: PARTIALLY INCORRECT — must be split by resource axis.
final_verdict.correct_version: STORAGE and WORK advantages require compression (K(f) bound). TIME, DEPTH, COMMUNICATION, and VERIFICATION advantages do NOT require compression — they can be achieved through parallelism, locality, or probabilistic checking.
what_survives: A1 (representation): every computation has a state [PROVEN]
what_fails: A3 (compactness): NOT necessary for time, depth, communication, verification [PROVEN]
K(f) as sole bound: K(f) bounds storage/work, NOT time/depth/communication [PROVEN]
Original closure theorem: too strong — claims compression is necessary for ALL advantage [DISPROVEN]
final_verdict.revised_theorem:
The closure theorem splits into 6 independent theorems:
  1. STORAGE: S(r) ≥ K(f). Compression necessary. [PROVEN]
  2. WORK: W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f). Compression necessary. [PROVEN]
  3. TIME: T(r) ≥ C(r)/P. Compression NOT necessary (parallelism). [PROVEN]
  4. DEPTH: D(r) ≥ log₂(C(r)). Compression NOT necessary (balancing). [PROVEN]
  5. COMMUNICATION: Comm(r) depends on layout. Compression NOT necessary. [PROVEN]
  6. VERIFICATION: V_cost can be O(log n) via PCP. Compression NOT necessary. [PROVEN]

Compression is necessary and sufficient ONLY for storage and work advantages. All other resource advantages can be achieved without compression.
